title: COBOL in Modern Mainframes and Global Banking Infrastructure
source_title: Reuters Special Report: The Global Financial Architecture Built on COBOL
content: Despite recurring predictions of its demise, COBOL remains the backbone of global commercial transaction processing. A 2022 survey by the Micro Focus Foundation and IT industry researchers estimated that over 800 billion lines of active COBOL code run daily in enterprise production environments. Approximately 95% of ATM swipes and 70% of global financial transaction systems rely on COBOL routines deployed on IBM zSystems mainframes running z/OS and CICS (Customer Information Control System). COBOL persists due to its fixed-point decimal arithmetic (COMP-3 packed decimal format) which eliminates binary floating-point rounding errors that can corrupt financial ledgers, as well as its massive record-processing throughput.
